flashcards.definition: The amount of substance containing $$6.022\times10^{23}$$ elementary entities, used to count particles by relating them to measurable mass.
The mass of one mole of a substance, typically expressed in $$\text{g/mol}$$, numerically equal to the sum of atomic masses in a formula.
The weighted mean of an element’s naturally occurring isotopes based on their relative abundances, reported in atomic mass units.
An analytical technique that ionizes particles and separates them according to $$m/z$$ to determine isotopic masses and relative abundances.
The fraction of atoms of a particular isotope in a natural sample, expressed as a percentage and used in weighted-average calculations.

multipleChoice.questionText: A sample of neon contains $$90.48\%$$ of an isotope with mass $$19.992\ \text{amu}$$, $$0.27\%$$ of an isotope with mass $$20.994\ \text{amu}$$, and $$9.25\%$$ of an isotope with mass $$21.991\ \text{amu}$$. What is the average atomic mass of neon?
A compound with molar mass $$180.16\ \text{g/mol}$$ has a sample mass of $$36.03\ \text{g}$$. How many molecules are present in the sample?

fillInTheBlank.questionText: In a mass spectrum, ions are separated on the basis of their ______ ratio.
If $$0.250\ \text{mol}$$ of atoms are present, the number of atoms is ______.

flashcards.definition: A notation showing how electrons are distributed among atomic orbitals in an atom or ion, following energy ordering and quantum rules.
A technique in which electromagnetic radiation ejects electrons from atoms, and the measured kinetic energies reveal relative binding energies.
The net positive attraction experienced by an electron after accounting for shielding by other electrons.
A measure of atom size based on distances between nuclei, which generally decreases across a period and increases down a group.
The energy required to remove the outermost electron from a gaseous atom in its ground state.

multipleChoice.questionText: Which species has the electron configuration $$1s^22s^22p^63s^23p^6$$?
The first ionization energy of aluminum is lower than that of magnesium primarily because the electron removed from aluminum is in a(n)
options: $$3p$$ orbital, which is higher in energy than a $$3s$$ orbital
$$3s$$ orbital, which is more shielded than a $$2p$$ orbital
$$3p$$ orbital, which penetrates closer to the nucleus than a $$3s$$ orbital
$$2p$$ orbital, which is fully filled and therefore easier to remove
multipleChoice.correctAnswer: $$3p$$ orbital, which is higher in energy than a $$3s$$ orbital

fillInTheBlank.questionText: In photoelectron spectroscopy, electrons with greater binding energy produce photoelectrons with ______ kinetic energy when the same frequency of light is used.
Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally ______ because the increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer while shielding changes little.
